alt: Two men stand behind the counter of a traditional coffeehouse, surrounded by rows of shisha pipes, hanging cups, glasses and plates.
caption: Photo: a coffeehouse (مَقْهَى) in Cairo, with tea in small glasses, shisha pipes on the shelves and the waiter (النَّادِل) behind the counter.

spots.note: Call him with لَوْ سَمَحْتَ (excuse me).
In the Levant it is called الْأَرْجِيلَة.
Singular: فِنْجَان, a small cup for coffee or tea.
Tea comes in a small glass; ask for شَاي بِنَعْنَاع, tea with mint.

alt: A white taxi drives along a sunny city street lined with tall apartment buildings, palm trees, shop signs and a few pedestrians.
caption: A street in Egypt: the taxi (التَّاكْسِي) waits in the road while people cross between the buildings and shop signs.

spots.note: Agree the fare first, or ask for the meter: الْعَدَّاد.
The sign reads صَيْدَلِيَّة, pharmacy.

alt: A breakfast seen from above on a wooden table: a round metal tray of small bowls with olives, labneh and zaatar, red teapots, a glass of tea, bread and a plate with cutlery.
caption: Photo: a Levantine breakfast (فُطُور): labneh, zaatar with oil, olives and bread, with tea (شَاي) poured from the red teapot.

spots.note: Served in a small glass; ask for it بِدُونِ سُكَّر, without sugar.
Thick strained yogurt, eaten with olive oil and bread.
A thyme and sesame mix; dip bread in oil, then in zaatar.
Manousheh: flatbread baked with cheese or zaatar.

alt: An empty clinic waiting room with black armchairs along a grey wall, a television, a glass door with an exit sign and a small wooden table with tissues and hand sanitizer.
caption: The waiting room (غُرْفَةُ الِانْتِظَار): sit down, and the receptionist (الْمُوَظَّفَة) will call your name.

spots.note: تَفَضَّلْ، اِجْلِسْ: please, sit down.
On signs in the Arab world you read مَخْرَج instead of EXIT.

credit.title: File:A waiting room at a medical healthcare clinic, doctor's office, hospital.jpg
credit.author: Harrison Keely

alt: A round patterned plate of mezze on a green tablecloth, seen from above: olives, hummus, a potato salad, pickles, green peppers and a yogurt dip.
caption: A plate of mezze (مَزَّة), the small dishes that start an Arab meal: hummus, olives, pickles and salads.

spots.note: Scoop it up with bread, never with a fork.
Pickled cucumber, served with most meals.
Ask: هَلْ هُوَ حَارّ؟ Is it hot?

credit.title: File:Syria, Al-Husn, Arabic meze or mezze.jpg
credit.author: Vyacheslav Argenberg

alt: Inside a dark old bakery, a baker in a long white robe carries a tray of bread on his shoulder as sunbeams fall through the roof beside a large oven.
caption: An old bakery (مَخْبَز) in Cairo: the baker (الْخَبَّاز) carries hot bread from the oven on a wooden tray.

spots.note: In Egypt people call bread عَيْش, which also means life.
The long loose robe many Egyptian men wear.

alt: Green bilingual street signs and a traffic light on a red signal stand on a pole in front of stone houses and trees in a hilly city.
caption: Photo: street signs in Amman. ش. is short for شَارِع (street). At the traffic light (الْإِشَارَة) ask: أَيْنَ…؟ Where is…?

spots.note: Directions often say: عِنْدَ الْإِشَارَة, at the traffic light.
Read the first word: ش. = شَارِع, street.
Pointing يَسَارًا, to the left.

alt: A crowded open-air clothes market on a city square: racks of clothing, stalls, shoppers and a black railing in front of old stone buildings on a hillside.
caption: Photo: an open-air clothes market (سُوق) in Amman. Ask the seller: بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟ How much is this?

spots.note: It is مُزْدَحِم, crowded.
The sign reads فُنْدُق سَن رَايْز, Sunrise Hotel.

credit.title: File:AmmanClothesMarked.jpg
credit.author: Niels Elgaard Larsen - (WT-en) Elgaard at English Wikivoyage

alt: An empty flat with a white fitted kitchen, a wooden floor, a square pillar in the middle, an open bathroom door and a single grey chair.
caption: An empty شَقَّة waiting for a tenant: the kitchen is fitted, the rest is up to you.

spots.note: A fitted kitchen often comes with the flat even when it is not furnished.
The same word is used for a wardrobe.
Wooden parquet; ask whether cleaning it is your job or the owner's.

credit.title: File:Empty apartment in Berlin with fitted kitchen and chair.jpg
credit.author: SmashingIt99

alt: A large traditional sitting room with floral sofas along the walls, patterned carpets, curtained windows, a wooden archway, a wall clock and a big tray of fruit on the floor.
caption: A majlis-style غُرْفَةُ الْجُلُوس: low seating all round and fruit for the guests.

spots.note: Hosts offer fruit after tea; take a little and say يَكْفِي، شُكْرًا when you have had enough.

credit.title: File:View of a traditional majlis in northern Qatar.jpg
credit.author: https://www.flickr.com/photos/lawrenceyeah/7081108559/in/album-72157629786342662/

alt: An airport baggage hall with an empty metal carousel, a lit sign above it, a display screen, a grey pillar and travellers waiting on the far side.
caption: The photo is an airport carousel; at Ramses Station there is none, so you go straight to مَكْتَبُ الْمَفْقُودَات (the lost-property office).

spots.note: At an airport this screen shows whose bags are coming; at a station, ask at the office.

credit.title: File:Baggage claim carousel 2 with display screen at Terminal 3 of Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ).jpg
credit.author: Silver Dovelet

alt: The rose-coloured facade of the Treasury at Petra carved into the cliff, with crowds of tourists and seated camels in the sandy square below.
caption: Photo: الْخَزْنَة in Petra, Jordan, a tomb facade carved straight into the rock. Faisal's trip was to Luxor and Aswan in Egypt.

spots.note: Al-Khazneh, the most famous facade in Petra.

alt: A small examination room with a wooden door, a padded examination bed covered with paper, a chair in the corner and medical equipment mounted on the grey wall.
caption: The examination room at a clinic. Sit down and tell the طَبِيب what hurts.

spots.note: The examination couch; the doctor may point to it and say تَفَضَّلِي (please).

credit.title: File:Exam room in a doctor's office.jpg
credit.author: Harrison Keely

alt: An old pharmacy shopfront on an Egyptian street with an Arabic sign, an open door, a window full of products, and a car, a motorbike and palm trees along the road.
caption: A neighbourhood صَيْدَلِيَّة. The green bowl-and-snake symbol marks pharmacies across the Arab world.

spots.note: It reads صَيْدَلِيَّة (pharmacy); the name is below in Latin letters.

alt: A garden birthday party: adults clap in the foreground while a small girl looks at a pink cake with one lit candle on a pink tablecloth, next to a coffee cup and a glass.
caption: حَفْلَةُ عِيدِ مِيلَاد in the garden: cake, one candle and everyone clapping.

spots.note: Everyone sings, then the child blows it out.

credit.title: File:Celebration of a birthday with cake and clapping hands at a party in a garden setting.jpg
credit.author: Shixart1985

alt: A sunny view over the Dead Sea from a hillside garden with a tall palm tree, pink flowering bushes, a parasol on the beach path, a small round pool and hazy mountains across the water.
caption: Blue sky and a warm بَحْر: the kind of day you plan the trip for.

spots.note: The hazy hills on the far shore.

alt: A large airport check-in hall with a row of counters and screens along the back wall, a maze of blue queue barriers in front and passengers waiting with their luggage.
caption: The check-in hall: find your airline on the شَاشَة, then wait in the طَابُور.

spots.note: The screen above each counter shows the flight number and destination.
The check-in counter; the clerk weighs your suitcase here.
Ask هَلْ هٰذَا هُوَ الطَّابُور؟ (is this the queue?) before you join it.
Most airlines allow 23 kilos; it goes on the مِيزَان (scales) at the counter.

alt: A hotel lobby at night with a long wooden reception desk, two computer screens on it, a green pendant lamp, big square ceiling lights, a green stool and stairs at the left.
caption: The lobby of a hotel: the مَكْتَبُ الِاسْتِقْبَال is where you ask for your key.

spots.note: Say لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، عِنْدِي حَجْز (excuse me, I have a booking).
The lift is الْمِصْعَد; the first floor is الطَّابِق الْأَوَّل.

credit.title: File:Reception desk at Hotel Holiday Inn Helsinki City Centre.jpg
credit.author: JIP

alt: A young woman in a dark jacket and glasses sits at a glass table with a sheet of paper in front of her, talking to an older woman seen from behind who is holding a pen.
caption: An interview: the مُدِيرَة asks the questions, and the السِّيرَة الذَّاتِيَّة lies on the table.

spots.note: A man applying is الْمُتَقَدِّم.
Address her as يَا سَيِّدَة (madam) or with her title.

alt: A woman sits at an office desk in front of an old computer monitor, with a telephone in the foreground, a printer and filing cabinet behind her and a green notice board covered in papers on the wall.
caption: A busy office: the مُوَظَّفَة answers the هَاتِف and checks the تَقْوِيم.

spots.note: Answer with آلُو (hello) on the phone.
Many people also say الْكُمْبْيُوتَر.

credit.title: File:Secretary at work.jpg
credit.author: Holy Trinity Lutheran Church, Thousand Oaks, California

alt: An older woman in a dark headscarf shapes a small round biscuit in her hands, with trays of unbaked kaʿk on the table beside her, a blue metal oven behind and a second woman working in the background.
caption: Making كَعْك for Eid: the biscuits go on the صِينِيَّة and into the فُرْن.

spots.note: A male neighbour is الْجَار; the saying goes الْجَارُ قَبْلَ الدَّار (choose the neighbour before the house).
Sweet Eid biscuits filled with dates or nuts and dusted with sugar.

alt: The faded art-deco front of an old cinema on a Cairo street, with film posters above the entrance, a tall vertical sign, a taxi and a grey car passing and a few people on the pavement.
caption: An old سِينِمَا in downtown Cairo: the مُلْصَق shows tonight's فِيلْم.

spots.note: The film poster: ask أَيُّ فِيلْم هٰذَا؟ (which film is this?).
Cairo taxis are white; agree the أُجْرَة (fare) or ask for the meter.

alt: The bright interior of a bank branch with a long wooden counter in the middle, tall glass windows with blinds looking out on green trees, hanging lamps, a queue barrier in the foreground and a blue sign on the right.
caption: Inside a بَنْك: wait behind the حَاجِز until the مُوَظَّف at the مَكْتَب calls you.

spots.note: Say أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَفْتَحَ حِسَابًا (I would like to open an account) here.

credit.title: File:Hancock Whitney Bank, Carrollton Branch, New Orleans March 2026 - 5.jpg
credit.author: Infrogmation

alt: A small wooden tourist police kiosk with a tiled roof stands on sandy ground at Petra; two police officers in blue stand in its doorway talking to tourists, while a donkey with a red saddle blanket waits at the left.
caption: Photo: a kiosk of the الشُّرْطَة السِّيَاحِيَّة at Petra. In Amman too, tell the شُرْطِيّ فَقَدْتُ هَاتِفِي (I lost my phone).

spots.note: Officers at the main sights; many speak some English.
Donkeys, horses and camels carry visitors through Petra; agree the price first.
The red-and-white checked headcloth worn in Jordan.

credit.title: File:Jordanian tourist police kiosk at Petra.jpg
credit.author: Faisal Case

alt: The tall main hall of the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, with a large dark stone statue on the left, white columns and an upper gallery, and visitors walking between glass display cases and stone sarcophagi.
caption: Photo: the main hall of the Egyptian Museum (الْمَتْحَفُ الْمِصْرِيّ) in Cairo, not the Jordan Museum of the dialogue: statues, columns and a gallery above.

spots.note: Ask هَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أُصَوِّرَ؟ before taking a photo.

alt: A sand-coloured post office building in Amman with the words Jordan Post on its facade in English and Arabic, an outside metal staircase, and a car park full of parked cars in front.
caption: Photo: Jordan Post (الْبَرِيدُ الْأُرْدُنِّيّ) in Amman, seen from across its car park. Faisal's post office in the dialogue is in Cairo.

spots.note: The sign reads الْبَرِيد الْأُرْدُنِّيّ, Jordan Post.

alt: Shoppers with trolleys crowd in front of the delicatessen and meat counter of a large supermarket in Cairo, under a dark ceiling hung with red advertising banners.
caption: The deli counter of a big Cairo supermarket on a busy evening: shoppers, trolleys (عَرَبَات) and offers (عُرُوض) everywhere.

credit.title: File:2011 deli Spinneys HyperMarket grocery Cairo 5384776750.jpg
credit.author: juliegomoll

alt: The open front of a small mobile phone shop: a glass display counter full of phone boxes on the left, racks of colourful phone covers inside, price lists on the right wall and a man leaning on the counter.
caption: A small phone shop (مَحَلُّ هَوَاتِف): SIM cards (شَرَائِح), covers and repairs under one roof.

spots.note: In Egypt a SIM card must be registered with your passport.

alt: A square white plate seen from above, filled with Lebanese dishes: tabbouleh, hummus, a fried kibbeh, lentils, roasted potatoes, a chickpea stew and creamy dips.
caption: A plate of Lebanese mezze (مَزَّة): most of it is vegetarian (نَبَاتِيّ), but ask about nuts and meat stock.

spots.note: Parsley, tomato and a little bulgur; naturally vegetarian.
Usually filled with minced meat and pine nuts, so ask هَلْ فِيهِ لَحْم؟

spots.en: the mutabbal (smoky aubergine dip with tahini)

alt: A large round metal platter of mansaf: pieces of lamb on the bone laid over yellow rice and scattered with fried almonds, standing on a patterned tablecloth.
caption: Mansaf (الْمَنْسَف), the national dish of Jordan: lamb cooked in dried yoghurt (جَمِيد) over rice, with almonds on top.

spots.note: Traditionally eaten with the right hand, بِالْيَدِ الْيُمْنَى.
Say عِنْدِي حَسَاسِيَّة مِنَ الْمُكَسَّرَات if you have a nut allergy.

alt: The ticket hall of a Cairo Metro station: a long blue counter with barred ticket windows, a clock above it, bright strip lights on a dark ceiling and a few passengers walking across the grey floor.
caption: The ticket hall (صَالَةُ التَّذَاكِر) of a Cairo Metro station; the ticket windows (شَبَابِيك) sell paper tickets.

spots.note: Say تَذْكِرَة وَاحِدَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ, one ticket, please.

alt: An empty classroom with cream walls, a long white board on the far wall, and rows of white desks with yellow-framed wooden chairs.
caption: An empty classroom (الصَّفّ) before the lesson: board, desks and chairs.
